## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

Sekhiya 36 of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga, titled *Odanappaṭicchādana* ("Covering with rice"), is a monastic training rule governing dining etiquette within the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates a monk's conduct while eating almsfood, prohibiting the practice of concealing curries or condiments beneath rice out of a desire to obtain more [SuttaCentral]. Modern English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
This training rule is widely shared across early Buddhist monastic codes. Curated parallels exist in the Pali Bhikkhu Pātimokkha, the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra, and the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Pātimokkha [SuttaCentral]. Outside the Theravāda tradition, parallels are preserved across Sanskrit, Classical Chinese, and Tibetan canonical transmissions, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya Vinayas, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral].
